components.css: :host{--g0:#0e0f0e;--g1:#171817;--g2:#232523;--g3:#3a3d3a;--g4:#7d817c;--g5:#a3a79f;--ink:#edeee8;--protein:#4f7cff;--carbs:#d2790e;--fat:#c8384b;--fiber:#3fad3e;--water:#299fcd;--caffeine:#854cdd;--alcohol:#b24c74;--alert:#ff6f91;--done:#3fcb7e;} .ds-macros{font-family:'Host Grotesk',system-ui,sans-serif;font-feature-settings:'tnum' 1;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);width:340px;background:var(--g0);border-bottom:1px solid var(--g2);} .ds-mc{font-family:'Host Grotesk',system-ui,sans-serif;font-feature-settings:'tnum' 1;padding:14px 12px;border:0;border-left:1px solid var(--g2);background:transparent;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;transition:background .15s;} .ds-mc:first-child{border-left:0;padding-left:0;} .ds-mc:hover{background:var(--g1);} .ds-mc p{margin:0;} .ds-ml{font-size:12px;color:var(--g4);} .ds-mv{font-size:22px;font-weight:500;} .ds-mt{margin-left:2px;font-size:12px;color:var(--g4);} .ds-bar{position:relative;height:3px;margin-top:10px;background:var(--g2);} .ds-bar i{position:absolute;inset:0 auto 0 0;} .ds-bar b{position:absolute;top:-4px;width:1px;height:11px;background:var(--g5);} .ds-mc:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--ink);outline-offset:-2px;}

narrative.overview:
Each day is one Swiss International Style poster set on a near-black ground. The single most important fact, how many kcal are left (or over), is set in enormous bold numerals flush left, and the rest of the day steps down a visible grid: a ruled row of macros on one absolute gram scale, ruled rows of details and drinks, then the meals as hairline rows. Concentric quarter arcs in the macro inks bleed off the top right edge, the only graphic flourish, and it carries data.

The palette is a fixed seven-step neutral ramp plus three macro inks used like poster printing plates, and one green that only ever means done. Type is one neo-grotesk, Host Grotesk, with tabular figures everywhere, so columns of numbers line up and days compare honestly. Depth is not a thing in this world: regions are divided by 1px hairlines, never lifted. On phones there are no boxes at all, one sheet divided by rules; on wider screens the secondary sections sit in quiet flat panels.

Density is planned, not packed. Every value has a fixed column and a fixed size, and state is shown by brightness on the ramp: the current meal burns in full ink, earlier ones step one ramp step down, empty ones sit two steps down. A food logged minutes ago stays lit with a small ink dot until it is seen.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground with a seven-step neutral ramp and no other greys.
Swiss poster in full colour: every nutrient area wears its own validated plate ink, with one warm alert colour for over and low.
One typeface, tabular figures, one huge number per screen.
1px hairlines in ramp step g2 instead of cards and shadows.
Primary actions set in ink, like the poster's type.

rules.name: The Seven Steps Rule
rules.body: The ramp g0 to ink is the only grey scale. No other neutral hex, no white or black alpha overlays standing in for a step.

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: A plate ink appears only on its own nutrient's data: value, bar, arc and source bars. Seven plates: protein, carbs, fat, fiber, water, caffeine, alcohol. A plate is never an error or "over" colour; sugar, salt and vitamins have no plate. Validated with validate_palette.js on g0.

rules.name: The Over In Alert Rule
rules.body: Over a limit, over a target or low on a goal is said with the word and the alert colour (#FF6F91) together: the kcal line reads "N over" in alert semibold while the figure stays ink; a limit cell shows "over" in alert beside its label and the overflow after the value, and its bar draws the overflow and tick in alert. Colour never carries it alone.

rules.name: The Green Means Done Rule
rules.body: Done Green marks completion only. It is not the primary action colour and does not mean "on track".

rules.name: The One Number Rule
rules.body: Each screen has one display-size number, and it answers the screen's question. Everything else is at least four times smaller.

rules.name: The Plain Label Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case at 12px in g4, sitting directly above their value. No uppercase tracked microlabels, no eyebrows above headings.

rules.name: The Hairline Not Box Rule
rules.body: On phones a section is a band between two rules, not a box. If you reach for a border on four sides, a radius and a fill, you are building a card; use a top rule instead.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: No `box-shadow` on any surface or control. State shows as a fill step (hover g1 or g2), an edge step (g3 to g5) or a brightness step in text.

dos: Do use only g0, g1, g2, g3, g4, g5 and ink for every neutral; g4 (#7D817C) is the lightest text allowed on g0 and g1 for small labels.
Do set primary actions in ink with g0 text, and name where the action lands ("Log food to lunch", "Log to lunch").
Do divide regions with 1px g2 hairlines and keep phone sections boxless.
Do keep tabular figures on and put each quantity in its own fixed column of an equal-fraction grid.
Do show over a limit or target in alert together with the word "over" (or "low"), never colour alone.
Do show state by stepping brightness on the ramp (current in ink, past in g5, empty in g4).
Do draw every macro bar on one absolute gram scale for the day, with a g5 tick at the target.
Do keep touch targets at 44px and list rows at 60px or more.
donts: Don't use a macro ink for anything other than that macro's own data; fat red is never an error or warning colour.
Don't use Done Green for buttons, links, progress or "on track".
Don't add box-shadows, gradients or tinted gradient tiles to any surface.
Don't introduce greys outside the seven-step ramp, or cyan, purple, pink and orange accents.
Don't put more than one display-size number on a screen.
Don't add uppercase tracked microlabels or eyebrows above headings; labels are plain 12px sentence case.
Don't wrap phone sections in rounded filled cards.
